questions.question: ….................. are the males of a bee colony. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Males carry the eggs in their brood pouch, which is deposited by the female with the help
  • of her ovipositor. Males take care of the eggs throughout the incubation period, lasting from 10
  • days to 6 weeks. They maintain controlled environment within its pouch for embryonic
  • development. It ensures optimal temperature & salinity inside the pouch, provide oxygen &
  • nutrients directly through the walls of the pouch. The eggs are also protected from predators. Once
  • the development is complete, they experience contractions & give birth to young ones. They
  • invest much of their time and energy for nurturing their young ones.

  • up slowly. Melanin pigment also dark colour in animals. Animals can also change its body colour
  • to regulate body temperature. Darkening the body colour helps to absorb more heat & lightening
  • reflects heat.

questions.question: What is the significance of the mother otter's role in teaching her pups to swim and hunt? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Whatisthesignificanceofthemotherotter’sroleinteachingherpupstoswimandhunt?
  • (U)(CO2)
  • Teaching survival skills is a crucial role played by mother otter. They gradually introduce
  • their pups into water, initially carrying them on their back before independent swimming. They
  • teach them swimming through playful interactions & supervised practice. Hunting skills are
  • taught by bringing prey live prey to the den & demonstrating techniques, allowing the pups to
  • practice & mimic these behaviours. Sea otters use tools to crack open shells. All these vital skills
  • are taught by the mother, which in turn increases the survival chances of the young ones.

questions.question: Describe how a new colony is formed in termites? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describehowanewcolonyisformedintermites?(U)(CO1)
  • New colonies are established by winged reproductive adults, known as alates. Alates
  • emerge from mature colonies and take flight during specific seasons to mate and create new nests.
  • With the arrival of rainy season, these winged males and females swarm out of their nests at night.
  • Many of them fall as prey to predators. A few alates will land, mate and initiate new nests. Upon
  • landing the winged termites shed their wings. Each male follows a female until they find a
  • suitable spot to dig a hole and start their nest. After mating, the newly formed king and Queen
  • establish a life-long partnership, beginning the gradual process of building a new colony. They dig
  • a small cell in the ground and the queen starts laying eggs. The King and Queen care for the eggs
  • and young at first. When there are enough workers, they take over these jobs. The queen directs
  • the workers to build the nest, using mud, soil, saliva and waste. The royal chamber houses the
  • King and Queen, protected by soldiers. Nearby, the brood chambers serve as nurseries where
  • workers care for eggs and nymphs, ensuring the colony’s future workforce and defenders. ( Give
  • fullmarksforanyrelevantpoints)

questions.question: Describe the different mechanisms employed by animals for faking / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describethedifferentmechanismsemployedbyanimalsforfaking.(U)(CO2)
  • a) By mimicking/ impersonate other animals – Eg: Mimic octopus mimic other animals like
  • lionfish, flatfish etc.
  • b) Camouflage – blending with the surroundings for avoiding detection by predators. Eg: Leaf
  • tailed Gecko
  • c) Brood parasitism – certain birds lay eggs in the nest of other birds. The host mistakes them as
  • their biological offsprings and raises the offsprings. Eg Cuckoo.
  • d) Pretending dead – certain animals when threatened, they limp, emit foul odour, drool & play
  • dead. Eg: Opposum.
  • e) Courtship display – male peacock spiders raise their colourful abdominal flap like a peacock’s
  • tail during courtship display.
  • f) Aggressive mimicry – Angler fish, uses their esca as lure to attract prey.
  • (Explanationofany4Points)

  • (b) Pair-living Society (e.g. Albatross, Swans, Penguins, Fox)
  • (c) Family Group (e.g. Elephants, Lions, Wolves)
  • (d) Harems (e.g., Gorillas, Horses, Sea lions)
  • (e) Matriarchal Society (e.g., Elephants, Bonobos, Spotted heynas)
  • (f) Hierarchical Society (e.g., Chickens, Wolves, Baboons, Macaques)
  • (g) Egalitarian Societ (e.g., Bonobos, Some bird flocks)
  • (h) Fission-fusion Society (e.g., Chimpanzees, Dolphins, some bats)
  • (i) Co-operative Breeding Society (e.g., Meerkats, African Wild dogs, Acorn Woodpeckers)
  • (j) Eusocial Society (e.g., Honey bees, Ants, Termites)
